claim: Human: DSPP encodes the major non-collagenous dentin matrix proteins made by odontoblasts; heterozygous DSPP mutations cause dentinogenesis imperfecta type 1/2 and dentin dysplasia (Xiao et al. 2001, Nat Genet). Odontoblasts persist and secrete dentin throughout adult life, so this is a constitutive adult non-reproductive function.
best_source: Xiao et al. 2001, Nat Genet 27:201-4, PMID 11175790, https://www.nature.com/articles/ng0201_201
verify_reason: The Xiao et al. 2001 abstract (PMID 11175790) confirms three DSPP mutations segregating with dentinogenesis imperfecta 1 in three Chinese families. This is human germline genetics, so it is gene-specific. Two caveats: the paper shows a developmental dentin disease, not adult expression, and the statement that odontoblasts keep secreting dentin through adult life is general dental biology the paper does not itself show. The mutations are dominant (splice-site and missense), not simple loss of function. Tooth is absent from every panel the screen uses, so the gap is real.
criteria_gap: Tooth/dental pulp is absent from the HPA and GTEx bulk panels, HPA single-cell clusters and the rare-cell screen (brain, eye, heart, lung, kidney, liver, pancreas, gut), so the catalog's 0.6 TPM maximum does not sample the tissue where DSPP is abundant. No literature review existed for this gene.

claim: Human dental pulp tissue and odontoblast-like cells express PANX3 mRNA and protein (RT-PCR and immunofluorescence), where it mediates ATP release on cold stimulus.
verify_reason: PMID 26263540 abstract states Panx3 mRNA and protein were found in human dental pulp tissue and cultured odontoblast-like cells by RT-PCR and immunofluorescence, and that Panx3 overexpression or shRNA changes cold-evoked ATP release. Caveats: the functional work is in cultured cells, donor age is not given in the abstract (pulp usually comes from extracted teeth of young adults), and it is a single unreplicated study.
criteria_gap: Tooth is not in any expression panel used by the screen.

claim: Human: RT-PCR on primary gingival keratinocytes from healthy subjects showed constitutive DEFB104 mRNA (Premratanachai et al. 2004).
best_source: PMID 14871351 (Premratanachai et al. 2004, Oral Microbiol Immunol 19:111, DOI 10.1111/j.0902-0055.2002.00127.x)
verify_reason: The PubMed abstract of PMID 14871351 states that keratinocytes from healthy subjects were analysed by RT-PCR and 'Constitutive mRNA expression was evident for DEFB-104, 107, 109, 111, and 112'. The claim is accurate as stated. Limits: these are cultured primary gingival keratinocytes, not intact tissue; the RT-PCR is qualitative so the level is unknown; donor age is not given in the abstract. I read the abstract only.
criteria_gap: Gingiva and oral mucosa are not in the HPA/GTEx bulk panels or the rare-cell screen. This is cultured-cell RT-PCR, so the expression level is unknown.

claim: Human: constitutive DEFB107 mRNA was detected by RT-PCR in cultured gingival keratinocytes from healthy subjects. UniProt otherwise lists it as testis-specific.
verify_reason: The abstract of PMID 14871351 lists DEFB-107 among genes with constitutive mRNA expression in gingival keratinocytes from healthy subjects by RT-PCR. UniProt Q8IZN7 says 'Specifically expressed in testis' but only by inference (ECO:0000305), so it does not contradict. Limits: cultured primary cells, qualitative RT-PCR, level unknown, abstract only. DEFB107A/B are identical copies.
criteria_gap: Gingival and oral epithelium are absent from the bulk panels and the rare-cell screen. The catalog shows 0.0 TPM off-target.

claim: Human: constitutive DEFB112 mRNA was detected by RT-PCR in cultured gingival keratinocytes from healthy subjects.
verify_reason: The abstract of PMID 14871351 lists DEFB-112 among genes with constitutive mRNA expression in gingival keratinocytes from healthy subjects by RT-PCR. Limits: cultured primary cells, qualitative RT-PCR with unknown level, abstract only. UniProt Q30KQ8 has no tissue-specificity annotation to compare against.
criteria_gap: Gingival and oral epithelium are not sampled by the bulk or rare-cell panels. The catalog shows 0.04 TPM off-target.

claim: Human: DEFB114 mRNA was induced in gingival keratinocytes by IL-1beta and Candida species, with no constitutive expression. UniProt otherwise records epididymal protein only.
verify_reason: The abstract of PMID 14871351 states 'DEFB-108 and 114 were induced by interleukin (IL)-1beta and Candida species', placing DEFB114 in the inducible, non-constitutive group. UniProt Q30KQ6 records only epididymal protein (PMID 23482568), as claimed. Limits: stimulated cultured keratinocytes, not tissue; qualitative RT-PCR; abstract only.
criteria_gap: This is infection- and cytokine-induced expression in a tissue absent from the panels. The catalog shows 0.0 TPM off-target.

claim: Human. Ensembl annotates this gene as a RAD51L3-RFFL readthrough. Its three protein isoforms are built almost entirely from RAD51D (UniProt O75771, DNA repair) sequence, and the longest (272 aa) continues into the C-terminal RING region of RFFL (UniProt Q8WZ73, E3 ubiquitin ligase rififylin). Only short junction or tail segments are unique, so most peptides are shared with two normally expressed proteins. This is a sequence comparison done in this session; I did not look up RAD51D or RFFL tissue expression.
best_source: https://rest.ensembl.org/sequence/id/ENSG00000267618?type=protein;multiple_sequences=1 ; https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O75771.fasta ; https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q8WZ73.fasta ; HPA RAD51D ENSG00000185379 and RFFL ENSG00000092871 (https://www.proteinatlas.org): both Low tissue specificity, detected in all, protein-level evidence
verify_reason: Could not refute. Ensembl describes ENSG00000267618 as 'RAD51L3-RFFL readthrough' (havana, protein_coding) with three protein products, which I re-fetched and aligned by eye against UniProt. (1) ENSP00000466834 (272 aa): after the initiator Met, residues match RAD51D (O75771) from about residue 171 (AEALRRIQ...) to 301 (...LAKSSRQ), then continue in RFFL (Q8WZ73) from SIDSEDSFVPG to the C-terminal RING end (...RAVHVFRS). It skips the RFFL segment VSGAEDQN, which may match another RFFL isoform, so the only unique peptides are those spanning the RAD51D/RFFL junction and possibly that skip. (2) ENSP00000467986 (128 aa): RAD51D sequence from MLDVLQEL to LAKSSRQ plus SIDS from RFFL. (3) ENSP00000464799 (204 aa): RAD51D from residue 120 (MAANVAHGL...) to SSRQ, skipping one RAD51D segment (TQDEEEQ then AEALRR), with a unique 20-aa tail ILSCGQPAATGSAWMDSLRRSH. One wording correction: the longest isoform is roughly half RAD51D and half RFFL rather than 'almost entirely RAD51D', but the claim does say it continues into the RFFL RING region, so the substance stands. The claim left parent expression unchecked; HPA lists both RAD51D (ENSG00000185379) and RFFL (ENSG00000092871) as 'Low tissue specificity', 'Detected in all', with protein-level evidence. Caveats: this is sequence identity, not an expression measurement of the readthrough, and it cannot distinguish the readthrough from its parents (gene_specific=false). The readthrough itself has transcript-level evidence only in HPA.
criteria_gap: Expression is measured on the readthrough gene ID only (1.5 TPM off-target). Sequence identity with the separately annotated parent genes RAD51D and RFFL is not considered, so normal-tissue presentation of the shared peptides is missed.

claim: Human. Ensembl annotates this gene as a novel LIPT1-MRPL30 readthrough, and its 131-aa protein (ENSP00000387111) is identical to the first 118 residues of MRPL30 (UniProt Q8TCC3, 161 aa); only the last 13 residues (FVVSSQLFLKCIA) are unique. MRPL30 is a mitochondrial ribosomal protein, so nearly every peptide from this candidate is also a normal self peptide. This is a sequence comparison done in this session, not a published expression result; I did not check MRPL30 expression itself.
best_source: https://rest.ensembl.org/sequence/id/ENSG00000273155?type=protein ; https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q8TCC3.fasta ; HPA MRPL30 ENSG00000185414 (https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000185414-MRPL30/tissue): Low tissue specificity, detected in all, protein-level evidence
verify_reason: Could not refute. Ensembl describes ENSG00000273155 as 'novel LIPT1-MRPL30 readthrough' (havana, protein_coding). Its only protein, ENSP00000387111 (131 aa), is identical to MRPL30 (UniProt Q8TCC3, 161 aa) over residues 1-118; it then diverges into a unique 13-aa tail, FVVSSQLFLKCIA, where MRPL30 continues IKPLKLPQ... I re-fetched both sequences and the claim holds exactly. The claim left MRPL30 expression unchecked; HPA lists MRPL30 (ENSG00000185414) as 'Low tissue specificity', 'Detected in all', with evidence at protein level, so the shared 118 residues are normal self sequence in essentially every adult tissue. Caveats: this is a sequence-identity argument, not an expression measurement of the readthrough transcript, and by its nature it cannot distinguish the readthrough from its parent (hence gene_specific=false). Only peptides overlapping the 13-residue tail or the junction at residue 118/119 would be candidate-specific, and the readthrough protein itself has transcript-level evidence only in HPA.
criteria_gap: The screen scores RNA assigned to the readthrough gene ID (1.8 TPM off-target). Reads and peptides shared with the parent gene MRPL30 are not attributed to it, so the protein-level overlap with a housekeeping protein is invisible. mapping_risk=True flags this but does not exclude it.

tissue: any herpesvirus-infected somatic tissue (not tissue-restricted; shown in cultured human cells only)
cell_type: herpesvirus-infected cells (cell type not named in the abstract)
claim: Human TRIM43 is strongly upregulated during herpesvirus infection (including KSHV reactivation) through the transcription factor DUX4, and acts as a centrosomal E3 ligase that degrades pericentrin to restrict herpesviruses (Full et al., Nat Microbiol 2019). UniProt Q96BQ3 curates this as 'induced by DUX4 during herpesvirus infection'. Evidence is from cell culture; the abstract gives no human tissue data.
best_source: PMID 30420784 (PMC6294671), Full et al., Nat Microbiol 2019;4:164-176, Fig. 1d-g, Supplementary Figs. 1c and 3a; UniProt Q96BQ3
verify_reason: The source exists and says what is claimed. The PubMed abstract of Full et al., Nat Microbiol 2019 states TRIM43 shows 'profound upregulation during herpesvirus infection as part of a germline-specific transcriptional program mediated by the transcription factor DUX4' and ubiquitinates pericentrin for proteasomal degradation; UniProt Q96BQ3 curates 'induced by DUX4 during herpesvirus infection'. The open-access full text (PMC6294671) is stronger than the claim's 'cell culture only': induction by HCMV in primary human foreskin fibroblasts, higher TRIM43 mRNA in HSV-1-positive versus HSV-1-negative patient bronchoalveolar lavage samples (18 vs 16), and TRIM43 protein moderate or high in 10 of 17 AIDS Kaposi sarcoma skin biopsies with minimal staining in healthy skin. The paper's own tissue qRT-PCR also reports very low ubiquitous mRNA with higher levels in brain, thymus and testis (Supplementary Fig. 3a). Caveats: this is infected or diseased tissue, not normal steady-state adult tissue, so it is an induced-expression flag only (HFF are neonatal, KS is a tumor in immunosuppressed patients). Paralog specificity is not established: the methods say the RNA-seq analysed TRIM43A, TRIM43B and TRIM43C together, and the qRT-PCR, siRNA and polyclonal antibody (ab80460) are unlikely to separate near-identical copies. Healthy skin was minimal, which limits the practical off-target concern to actively infected cells.
criteria_gap: Every layer of the screen (bulk HPA/GTEx, single-cell clusters, IHC, rare-cell donor screen) measures steady-state uninfected tissue, so infection-induced expression is invisible; off-target TPM is 0.4. Herpesvirus latency and reactivation are common in adults. Coverage caveat for this whole batch: the session's web-search budget ran out after one search, so the other 24 labels were checked only against curated UniProt entries, not a literature search.

claim: Panx3 is expressed in mammalian epidermis and regulated during keratinocyte differentiation; global Panx3-knockout mice have thinner dermis and hypodermis, reduced epidermal barrier function and more dermatitis with age, and show delayed wound healing. TNF-alpha induces PANX3 in human HaCaT keratinocytes.
verify_reason: The sources say what is claimed. PMID 36813158: knockout mice have reduced dermal and hypodermal area, reduced barrier function and more dermatitis with age. PMID 30389492: delayed wound healing in knockouts and TNF-alpha induction in HaCaT. Human normal-skin evidence comes from PMID 22947051, which reports PANX3 protein in human epidermis, hair follicles, sebaceous and eccrine glands and blood vessels. Caveats: the human evidence is antibody staining (diffuse intracellular, with a ~70 kDa species whose identity needed separate confirmation), and the functional data are mouse.
criteria_gap: Bulk skin RNA is low (catalog max 3.0 nTPM elsewhere); expression rises with age and is induced by wounding and inflammation, which steady-state atlases do not capture. Skin is not in the rare-cell screen.

claim: Human: IHC across 70 normal tissues found cytoplasmic PRAME staining in sebaceous glands of the skin; a second review reports the same in sebocytes, consistently with clone EPR20330 but not with all anti-PRAME antibodies, and calls its significance unclear. Staining is cytoplasmic, not the nuclear pattern scored in tumors, so it may be clone-specific cross-reactivity.
verify_reason: Both sources say this. Kaczorowski 2022 (70 normal tissues): 'Cytoplasmic staining was seen in sebaceous glands of the skin whereas other cutaneous structures were negative'. Lezcano 2021: cytoplasmic staining of sebocytes, 'consistently observed with the EPR20330 clone, but not with all anti-PRAME antibodies', significance unclear. One addition to the claim: the 2022 study used a different clone (EP461, with E7I1B giving nearly identical patterns), so the staining is seen with more than one clone. It is still cytoplasmic rather than the nuclear pattern, has no RNA or knockout validation, and cross-reactivity is not excluded, so it is not gene-specific proof of PRAME protein.
criteria_gap: Sebaceous gland is a small fraction of bulk skin RNA and is not among the tissues in the donor-level rare-cell screen (brain, eye, heart, lung, kidney, liver, pancreas, gut).

claim: Human: the readthrough protein (UniProt K7ELQ4, 463 aa) is identical to canonical ATF7 (P17544) over its first 411 residues and shares no segment of 8+ residues with the NPFF precursor (O15130), by direct sequence comparison in this session. HPA classes ATF7 as 'low tissue specificity, detected in all', so nearly every peptide from this candidate is also made by a ubiquitously expressed transcription factor.
source: https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/K7ELQ4.fasta (compared with P17544 and O15130); HPA ENSG00000170653
verify_reason: Re-ran the comparison on the UniProt FASTA files: K7ELQ4 is 463 aa and identical to ATF7 (P17544, 483 aa) over residues 1-411 (88.8%). It shares no 8-mer with the NPFF precursor O15130. 403 of its 455 possible 9-mers are also ATF7 9-mers; only the 52-residue C-terminal tail is unique. The HPA ATF7 page reads 'Low tissue specificity' and 'Detected in all'. The expression evidence is for ATF7, not the readthrough transcript, so this is a peptide-sharing problem and not evidence that the readthrough gene itself is expressed.
criteria_gap: The screen scores the readthrough gene's own RNA (HPA: not detected; 5.6 TPM blood). The mapping_risk flag does not capture that 89% of the protein is shared with ATF7, so the gene-level RNA value understates normal-tissue presentation of its peptides.

claim: Human: a homozygous SP7/Osterix frameshift (c.1052delA) causes recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (OI type XII) with recurrent fractures, bone deformity and delayed tooth eruption; UniProt curates SP7 as a transcriptional activator essential for osteoblast differentiation, with expression restricted to bone-derived cells.
best_source: PMID 20579626 (Lapunzina 2010, Am J Hum Genet); UniProt Q8TDD2; PMID 15474293 (Gao 2004, Gene) for the limits of the human expression data
verify_reason: PMID 20579626 exists and says what is claimed: homozygous c.1052delA in SP7/OSX in an Egyptian child with recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (recurrent fractures, mild bone deformities, delayed tooth eruption). UniProt Q8TDD2 does say 'essential for osteoblast differentiation' and 'Restricted to bone-derived cell'. Two caveats. The patient is a child and the paper frames it as bone development, so this is human loss-of-function evidence, not adult expression evidence. UniProt's tissue line rests on PMID 15474293, where SP7 mRNA was restricted to bone-derived cell lines in vitro and was undetectable by Northern in any adult tissue including mandibular bone; in vivo osteoblast expression was shown only by in situ on human embryonic tissue. So direct adult human expression is not shown by these sources. SP7 has no close paralog confusion here (genetic mapping plus sequencing).
criteria_gap: Bone, osteoblasts/osteocytes and teeth are absent from the bulk RNA panels, the HPA IHC set and the rare-cell screen (brain, eye, heart, lung, kidney, liver, pancreas, gut), so a bone-lineage master regulator reads as near-zero off-target (1.6 TPM, white matter). SP7 was not among the ~99 literature-reviewed proteins.

claim: Human: the Human Protein Atlas single-cell page lists CAGE1 as 'cell type enriched' in skeletal myofibers at the protein level in its deep visual proteomics data (protein tau 1.00), with no matching RNA value reported. This is a single atlas annotation with no primary paper found.
verify_reason: The HPA single-cell page was opened and does list protein specificity 'Cell type enriched (Skeletal myofibers)' with protein tau 1.00 in its deep visual proteomics section. One detail of the claim is wrong: that section does report RNA values (RNA tau 0.70, 'Cell type enhanced (T-cells)'); the gene-level single-cell RNA call is group enriched in early spermatids and late primary spermatocytes (tau 0.84). Weakened because this is a single atlas annotation with no primary paper, the supporting peptides and their uniqueness could not be inspected, and a tau of 1.00 may simply mean the protein was detected in only one profiled cell type in a sparse dataset. Gene specificity is unverified, and the gene is already flagged mapping_risk. Adult normal status of the tissue is assumed from HPA practice, not checked.
criteria_gap: The screen reads HPA RNA and immunohistochemistry but not the HPA mass-spectrometry (deep visual proteomics) cell-type layer; the existing literature verdict is no_normal_expression_evidence and the gene is flagged mapping_risk.

claim: Mouse: Cer1 is expressed in bone and growth plate by RT-PCR, immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridisation. Human: a nonsynonymous CER1 SNP (rs3747532) is associated with low bone mineral density and vertebral fracture in southern Chinese women. No adult human expression data were found.
verify_reason: PubMed abstract of PMID 19113921 (Tang et al., J Bone Miner Res 2009) read and matches: Cer1 expression in mouse bone and growth plate by RT-PCR, IHC and in situ hybridisation; human nonsynonymous SNP rs3747532 associated with low BMD in premenopausal women (OR 2.2, 95% CI 1.0-4.6, borderline) and vertebral fracture (OR 1.82, p = 0.025) in a 1083-subject cohort. Expression is mouse only (age of the mice not stated in the abstract; growth plate implies young animals), and the human link is a weak single-cohort candidate-gene association, not expression or function in adult human bone.
criteria_gap: Bone and growth plate are not in the bulk panels or the rare-cell screen; no literature verdict. The expression is mouse only and the human link is a genetic association.

claim: Human: Lin et al. 2002 detected CSAGE (CSAG1) and TRAG-3 by RT-PCR in normal cartilage as well as testis, but in no other normal tissue; OMIM 300944 records one study finding it absent from normal cartilage and another finding it in normal chondrocytes.
verify_reason: PubMed abstract of PMID 12039054 (Lin et al., Gene 2002) read: 'CSAGE and TRAG-3 are expressed in chondrosarcoma, melanoma, and cartilage and testis, but not in other normal tissues.' UniProt Q6PB30 repeats this, citing the same paper. So the source says it, in human. Weakened because: only the abstract was read, so donor age and how normal the cartilage was are unverified; the gene was cloned by differential display between chondrosarcoma lines and normal cartilage, which implies lower expression in cartilage; RT-PCR within a highly homologous family (CSAGE vs TRAG-3, with splice variants) may not separate paralogs; it is a single 2002 study with no replication found. The OMIM 300944 statement about conflicting studies could not be checked.
criteria_gap: Cartilage is not in any RNA panel or the rare-cell screen. The existing verdict specialized_tissue_expression may already reflect this. Read from a search-result abstract summary only; the OMIM page returned 403.

claim: Human: TRAG-3 (CSAG2/CSAG3) was detected by RT-PCR in normal cartilage alongside CSAGE in the Lin et al. 2002 study, and UniProt Q9Y5P2 lists it as weakly expressed in kidney. CSAG2/CSAG3 aliases overlap, so which paralog was assayed is uncertain.
verify_reason: The abstract of PMID 12039054 does say TRAG-3 is expressed in cartilage and testis but in no other normal tissue, and UniProt Q9Y5P2 does say 'Weakly expressed in kidney' (with no citation attached to that line). Weakened because the two sources disagree with each other on kidney (Lin et al. report no other normal tissue); TRAG-3 maps to the near-identical CSAG2/CSAG3 pair (one merged UniProt entry), so the assay cannot be assigned to CSAG2, and separation from CSAGE/CSAG1 by RT-PCR is unverified; only the abstract was read; single unreplicated 2002 study.
criteria_gap: Cartilage is not in the bulk panels or the rare-cell screen; CSAG2 has no literature verdict and is flagged as a mapping risk. The paper was read only as a search-result abstract summary; the UniProt entry was opened.

claim: Human articular chondrocytes express IL36B (IL-1F8) constitutively, per the UniProt induction annotation citing Magne 2006. UniProt also lists low-level expression in bone marrow, heart, lung and colon (PMIDs 20300079, 21242515, not opened).
source: PMID 16646978 (abstract read; the 'constitutive in articular chondrocytes' statement is from the UniProt IL36B entry citing this paper)
verify_reason: Magne 2006 does say IL-1F8 mRNA is constitutive in human articular chondrocytes (real-time PCR, six cultures). But these are isolated primary cells in culture from joint-replacement patients (osteoarthritis or femoral neck fracture; the paper does not say which group supplied each experiment), levels are reported only relative to the within-experiment maximum, and IL-1F8 protein was undetectable in chondrocyte supernatants. The authors conclude the joint is not a major source of IL-1F8. The UniProt low-level tissue list (PMIDs 20300079, 21242515) was confirmed only as a UniProt annotation; those papers were not opened.
criteria_gap: Cartilage and chondrocytes are absent from the HPA/GTEx bulk panels, the single-cell clusters and the rare-cell screen organs.

claim: Human NEU2 (cytosolic sialidase) is curated in UniProt (Q9Y3R4) as expressed in skeletal muscle, fetal liver and the NT2-D1 embryonal carcinoma line, based on the original cloning papers (PMID 10191093, PMID 10561456). The enzyme hydrolyses gangliosides and sialylated oligosaccharides.
best_source: PMID 23068092 (BBRC 2012, title only); original claim PMID 10191093
verify_reason: The cloning paper exists and says it: PMID 10191093 abstract, 'Northern blot analysis revealed expression of the NEU2 transcript only in skeletal muscle'. That is a single 1999 Northern blot. The second cited paper (PMID 10561456) is about expression in COS7 cells and E. coli; its abstract has no tissue data, and the 'fetal liver / NT2-D1' wording was not found in either abstract nor in the part of the UniProt entry retrieved. A later paper is titled 'Human cytosolic sialidase NEU2 - low general tissue expression but involvement in PC-3 prostate cancer cell survival' (PMID 23068092, BBRC 2012; title only, not opened), which by its title agrees with the atlases and not with the Northern blot. The skeletal muscle claim is therefore real but old and disputed. A 2022 mouse Neu2 knockout paper (PMID 35217678, title only) reports impaired muscle function, which is mouse-only.
criteria_gap: Skeletal muscle is in the bulk panels, but the atlases put the maximum off-target value in skin (2.13 TPM). The gene-specific cloning report of muscle expression therefore conflicts with the RNA atlases and has not been literature-reviewed. The category is 'Cancer Antigen only' with reproductive_best 0, so there is no reproductive rationale.

cell_type: osteoclasts and foreign body giant cells (macrophage lineage)
claim: UniProt (Q9BR26) curates OCSTAMP, by similarity to mouse, as a probable cell-surface receptor that cooperates with DCSTAMP in cell-cell fusion of osteoclasts and foreign body giant cells, promotes osteoclast differentiation and is involved in bone resorption. A 2026 paper title (PMID 41369694, not opened) states the same cooperative role.
verify_reason: UniProt Q9BR26 says what is claimed, but tagged 'By similarity' (ECO:0000250), with no human experimental reference, no tissue specificity annotation, and HPA 'Not detected'. PMID 41369694 (J Bone Miner Metab 2026) abstract opened: it is entirely mouse (DC-STAMP KO, OC-STAMP KO and double-knockout mice and their progenitor cells), showing the two proteins cooperate in osteoclast and FBGC fusion. So the function is well supported in mouse by knockout, but there is no human normal-tissue evidence in the cited sources. A PubMed search surfaced only disease-context human titles (silicosis, multiple myeloma), not opened.
criteria_gap: Bone and osteoclasts are absent from the bulk tissue panels and from the rare-cell screen, and expression is induced during osteoclast differentiation and macrophage fusion rather than constitutive. It is a multipass surface protein in normal bone remodelling. The human annotation is by similarity only.

claim: Panx3 is an ER calcium channel and hemichannel that promotes osteoblast and chondrocyte differentiation; mouse knockouts have altered long-bone growth and altered susceptibility to osteoarthritis and disc degeneration. Mostly mouse data; UniProt assigns the function to human by similarity, and human noncoding PANX3 variants associate with chronic back pain.
verify_reason: Sources exist, but the evidence is mouse and largely developmental. PMID 21690309 uses C2C12 and primary calvarial cells and metatarsal explants. PMID 26138248 states global Panx3 deletion gives no overt phenotype and no obvious effect on early skeletal development; PMID 26749194 and 33426805 report only shorter long bones, plus opposite effects on injury-induced versus ageing osteoarthritis. Human evidence is immunostaining in osteoarthritic lesions (disease tissue) and a noncoding-variant association with back pain (PMID 36448979). UniProt Q96QZ0 assigns the function by similarity.
criteria_gap: Bone and cartilage are absent from the HPA/GTEx bulk panels and from the rare-cell screen.

claim: Immunoblotting detected PANX3 species in adult human skeletal muscle tissue and in primary human myoblasts, where it regulates proliferation and differentiation. Antibody-based; the paper notes several immunoreactive species.
verify_reason: PMID 25239622 exists and says Panx3 is present in adult human skeletal muscle and primary myoblasts. The evidence is immunoblot with several immunoreactive species, including a ~70 kDa band the authors describe only as 'likely' modified Panx3; the functional work is in cultured myoblasts. No RNA or in situ confirmation in muscle tissue is cited, so the tissue claim rests on antibody specificity. In the cochlea paper (PMID 19009624) Panx3 labelling was only in cochlear bone, in mouse and rat.
criteria_gap: Protein-level claim despite low bulk muscle RNA; skeletal muscle is not in the rare-cell screen. Mouse/rat cochlea expression is also reported (PMID 19009624) but knockouts hear normally.

tissue: kidney, colon, small intestine, stomach, skeletal muscle
claim: Human: PRR5-ARHGAP8 is a readthrough locus with no function or tissue annotation of its own in UniProt (B1AHC3, B1AHC4). Its downstream parent ARHGAP8 (UniProt P85298) is 'highly expressed in kidney and placenta' and also in colon, skeletal muscle, small intestine and stomach (Johnstone et al., Gene 2004). Any peptide from the ARHGAP8 portion of the fusion would therefore be presented in normal kidney and gut.
best_source: UniProt P85298 (ARHGAP8); Johnstone CN et al., Gene 2004;336(1):59-71, PMID 15225876 (parent gene only)
verify_reason: The sources say what is claimed, but about the parent gene, not this one. UniProt P85298 (ARHGAP8) reads 'Highly expressed in kidney and placenta. Also expressed in colon, skeletal muscle, small intestine, stomach, and testis. Not detected in brain, liver or spleen', citing Johnstone et al. 2004 (PMID 15225876), whose abstract confirms transcripts in normal mammary gland and colon. The readthrough entries (B1AHC3, B1AHC4, H0Y9T8) are unreviewed with no function or tissue annotation. There is no direct evidence that the fusion transcript or protein exists in normal tissue. The valid point is narrower: peptides from the ARHGAP8-derived sequence are shared with a parent gene expressed in normal kidney and gut, which is a sequence-overlap (mapping_risk) issue rather than a missed function of the readthrough gene. I did not check the degree of sequence overlap.
criteria_gap: The screen scores the readthrough gene ID on its own (1.6 TPM thyroid; mapping_risk is already True), but quantifiers assign most shared-exon reads to the parent genes PRR5 and ARHGAP8. The protein sequence overlaps broadly expressed parents, so the low readthrough TPM understates normal-tissue exposure. This is inferred from the parent gene, with no direct evidence for the fusion protein.

claim: Mouse: postnatal conditional deletion of Osx (Sp7) at several time points showed it is essential for osteoblast differentiation and new bone formation in growing and adult bones, and severely disrupted osteocyte maturation, morphology and function. This is an adult homeostatic role, not only an embryonic one.
verify_reason: The source is real and accurately quoted: PMID 20615976 reports that postnatal conditional deletion of Osx at several time points blocks osteoblast differentiation and new bone formation in growing and adult bones and disrupts osteocyte maturation, morphology and function. Weakened only because it is mouse-only; it is a gene-specific conditional knockout and does show an adult, not just embryonic, role. No human adult data in this source.
criteria_gap: Shows the function is ongoing in adult bone, so it cannot be dismissed as developmental; bone is not sampled by any current expression layer.

claim: Mouse: Adig is predominantly expressed in the adipocyte fraction of adipose tissue (and testis); Adig-null mice show altered fat mass accrual and impaired leptin secretion, and a later study reports adipocyte-specific knockout disrupts lipid droplet formation in brown fat with impaired cold tolerance. Human: no adipose expression confirmed here (HPA and NCBI call human ADIG testis-enriched), though the knockout paper cites a human GWAS linking ADIG to BMI-adjusted leptin.
source: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7966854/ (Adig null mice, Cell Reports 2021); seipin/lipid droplet work: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.07.25.605195.full.pdf
best_source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7966854/ (mouse); GTEx v8 median expression for ENSG00000182035.11 via gtexportal.org API (human, adipose near zero)
verify_reason: The Cell Reports 2021 paper (PMC7966854) exists and says what is claimed: mouse Adig is most highly expressed in adipose tissue, mainly the adipocyte fraction, and Adig-null mice are leaner on a high-fat diet with reduced fat-mass-adjusted leptin and impaired leptin secretion from explants. All of it is mouse knockout work. The only human data is a GWAS locus near ADIG for BMI-adjusted leptin, where the implicated SNP (rs6071166, near SLC32A1) was not linked to expression of nearby genes in human adipose. I queried GTEx v8 directly: ADIG median is 86.6 TPM in testis, 1.2 in thyroid, and no adipose or breast tissue appears in the top 12 (all others at or below 0.14 TPM). HPA calls it testis-enriched with no protein data. UniProt's human entry describes a seipin-binding lipid-droplet function, but gives no human tissue evidence. The bioRxiv brown-fat/cold-tolerance source was not opened. No human adult adipose expression is supported.
criteria_gap: The screen is human RNA only, so a mouse adipocyte function is invisible to it. The row is also flagged mapping_risk, so the low human adipose value may be worth re-checking against GTEx adipose and breast directly; I could not retrieve those numbers.

claim: Mouse: BTN1A1 is required for milk lipid secretion (null mice release lipid droplets with damaged membranes, per OMIM 601610 summarising Ogg et al. 2004), and transcripts are also present in virgin mammary tissue. UniProt annotates the human protein for milk-fat droplet secretion by similarity.
verify_reason: The knockout requirement for milk-lipid droplet secretion is real and gene-specific, but it is mouse. PMID 20208008 only restates it; the primary source is Ogg et al. 2004 (PMID 15226505, title verified). UniProt gives the human function 'by similarity'. Whether this is a gap depends on policy: lactation is a reproductive-cycle function and the catalog already seems to count breast as reproductive. The virgin mammary transcripts are also mouse-only in the cited source.
criteria_gap: Only a gap if breast is counted among the excluded reproductive tissues (reproductive_best 1162 suggests it is). Adult female mammary epithelium is not disposable, and expression is strongly induced by lactation, which resting-tissue atlases undersample. The OMIM knockout detail was seen only as a search summary.

claim: Human: UniProt (Q8NET1, citing PMID 12600824) records testis-specific expression with low expression also detected in liver by cDNA-panel PCR.
verify_reason: UniProt Q8NET1 does say 'Specifically expressed in testis. Low expression is detected also in liver', citing PMID 12600824. The abstract of that paper does not mention liver and I could not open the full text, so the primary evidence is unverified. The signal is described as low, from cDNA-panel PCR, and primer specificity among DEFB108 copies is not established.
criteria_gap: The catalog's highest off-target value is 1.44 TPM in blood, and liver is not flagged. The gene carries a mapping-risk flag, so atlas quantification may be unreliable.

claim: Human: Zhang et al. 2014 (Development), summarising earlier RT-PCR work, state that DMRT6/DMRTB1 is strongly expressed in adult testis and weakly in human adult ovary and pancreas; in mouse, fetal Dmrt6 mRNA is mainly in brain. The mouse knockout phenotype is confined to spermatogonial differentiation and meiosis, with no somatic requirement reported.
best_source: Ottolenghi et al. 2002, Genomics 79:333-43, PMID 11863363 (primary, full text not opened); cited in Zhang et al. 2014, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4197572
verify_reason: Zhang et al. 2014 (PMC4197572) does say Dmrt6 'is strongly expressed in adult testis in mouse and human and weakly in human adult ovary and pancreas', citing Ottolenghi et al. 2002 (Genomics, PMID 11863363). That is a secondary one-line citation. The Ottolenghi abstract does not mention tissue expression and I could not open its full text, so the assay, its specificity among DM-domain paralogs and whether it was quantitative are unverified. The same paper reports Dmrt6 knockout mice as 'otherwise normal and healthy' outside spermatogenesis, with females normal and fertile, so there is no somatic function. Pancreas is already sampled by the bulk and rare-cell panels at about zero, so this is a weak, unreplicated 2002 RT-PCR signal.
criteria_gap: Gene-specific RT-PCR reporting weak pancreas signal where the atlases show about 0.3 TPM maximum (thyroid); pancreas is covered by bulk and rare-cell panels, so this is a low-priority discrepancy rather than an unsampled tissue.

claim: Mouse: GFRalpha4 is produced only in thyroid C cells and they express functional receptor throughout postnatal development. Knockout mice have 60% less thyroid calcitonin as newborns and increased juvenile bone formation, but adult calcitonin levels, C-cell number, growth and viability are normal.
verify_reason: Abstract of PMID 16497798 read and it matches the claim: by in situ and immunohistochemistry the functional GPI-anchored GFRalpha4 is made in mouse only in C cells (not parathyroid or brain); knockouts have 60% less thyroid calcitonin as newborns and 45% less at 3 weeks, increased juvenile bone formation, and normal adult calcitonin, C-cell number, growth and viability. Mouse only, hence weakened. It supports the human C-cell finding and shows the adult loss-of-function phenotype is mild.
criteria_gap: Rare endocrine cell type in an organ outside the rare-cell screen; knockout data are not used by the screen. The adult phenotype is mild, which argues the on-target risk is limited to C cells.

claim: Hes3 is expressed in adult human and rodent pancreatic islets. In mouse, Hes3-null animals show worse beta-cell loss and hyperglycaemia after streptozotocin, expression rises after islet damage, and knockdown in MIN6 cells reduces Pdx1, insulin expression and insulin release.
verify_reason: The abstract of PMID 25371201 confirms 'Hes3 is expressed in human and rodent pancreatic islets', mouse co-localisation with alpha and beta cell markers, MIN6 knockdown reducing Pdx1, insulin and evoked insulin release, and increased streptozotocin islet damage in Hes3-null mice. All functional and knockout data are mouse or a mouse insulinoma line. I could not get the full text (JBC returned 403, PMC blocked), so the assay and donor status for the human islet expression, and the claim that expression rises after islet damage, are unverified. Human evidence is a single statement from one lab.
criteria_gap: Islets are a small fraction of bulk pancreas, so bulk TPM dilutes them. The rare-cell screen covered pancreas but HES3 was 'below_screen'. Damage-induced (regenerative) expression is not captured by steady-state atlases. No literature review existed for this gene.

claim: Human: UniProt curates MAGEA11 as expressed in testis, ovary, prostate, breast and adrenal tissue, citing Bai 2005, whose abstract states MAGE-11 is expressed in androgen-dependent tissues and acts as an androgen receptor coregulator. Adrenal is the non-reproductive site of concern; I did not see expression levels.
best_source: PMID 15684378, full text PMC548016 (Fig. 12B and Discussion)
verify_reason: Bai 2005 (PMID 15684378, full text PMC548016) supports the UniProt annotation: 'MAGE-11 mRNA was also expressed in samples from testis, ovary, prostate, cancerous prostate, breast, and adrenal tissue, but was weak to undetectable in liver and lung' (Fig. 12B, adult human tissue RNA). The assay is weak, though: non-quantitative end-point RT-PCR at 35 cycles amplifying a 168-bp fragment, with no amplicon sequencing mentioned in the passages I read. The authors state the mRNA 'was not detectable by Northern blotting and required RT-PCR methods', even in testis, 'suggesting that MAGE-11 expression is low'. No protein was shown in normal adrenal, and a 168-bp amplicon in the highly homologous MAGE-A family leaves some paralog risk. Adrenal is the only clearly non-reproductive site; the signal is real but very low and unquantified, consistent with the atlas value near zero.
criteria_gap: The catalog's highest off-target is 0.15 TPM in oesophagus, so the atlases do not show the adrenal, prostate or breast expression reported by a gene-specific assay. Expression may be hormone-dependent and low; needs a check of whether prostate and breast are counted as reproductive in the screen.

claim: Mouse and human: OR4M1 (mouse Olfr734) is described as the hepatic receptor for the fasting hormone asprosin, mediating its glucogenic effect; liver knockdown of Olfr734 in diet-induced obese mice increased hepatic lipid content, and OR4M1 was reported as measurable and higher in human liver biopsies from men with type 2 diabetes. The abstract does not say whether the human measurement was RNA or protein.
best_source: PMID 40806011 (PMC12348634) for the human biopsy data; the underlying receptor claim is the mouse Olfr734 study by Li et al., Cell Metab 2019 (PMID 31230984, cited from memory, not opened here)
verify_reason: The source exists and says roughly this, but the human evidence is weaker than normal-tissue expression. Full text (PMC12348634): the functional data are mouse Olfr734 liver knockdown, plus OR4M1 siRNA in the immortalised human hepatocyte line THLE-2. The human measurement is mRNA (the discussion says 'mRNA levels of OR4M1'), in liver biopsies from patients with obesity with or without type 2 diabetes; there is no normal-liver group, so it is disease tissue. It is qPCR of a single-exon gene with a near-identical paralog (OR4M2), with no amplicon sequencing or protein data that I found. The 2020 review (PMID 32198197) states asprosin acts through OR4M1 in liver, but this rests on the mouse Olfr734 work, not a human assay. HPA/GTEx liver RNA near zero is not contradicted by any gene-specific human normal-tissue assay.
criteria_gap: Bulk liver RNA is about zero in HPA/GTEx (catalog max 0.06 TPM, in blood), so the screen sees nothing. The claim rests on mouse ortholog function plus a low-level human liver measurement. mapping_risk is True (OR4M1/OR4M2 paralogs), which could hide or confuse reads.

claim: Mouse only: Or5v1/Olfr110 is an oxylipin (12(S)-HEPE) receptor that drives hepatic fatty acid oxidation via PKA/ATF2/CPT1A; whole-body knockout mice develop impaired glucose control, weight gain, fatty liver and insulin resistance, and liver-specific deletion also impairs glucose control (Ge et al., Cell 2026). UniProt transfers this function to human OR5V1 (Q9UGF6) by similarity only; no human liver expression or protein data was found.
source: PMID 41570820 (cited in UniProt A2RT31, https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/A2RT31.txt; human entry https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9UGF6.txt)
best_source: PMID 41570820, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2025.12.016; UniProt A2RT31 (mouse, experimental) and Q9UGF6 (human, by similarity only)
verify_reason: The source exists and says what the claim reports, but the evidence is mouse-only. PubMed abstract of PMID 41570820 (Ge et al., Cell 2026;189:1481-1498, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2025.12.016) states that systemic or liver-specific Or5v1/Olfr110 deficiency impaired glucose homeostasis and that 12(S)-HEPE acts through Gs-PKA-pATF2-Cpt1a to promote fatty acid oxidation in liver. UniProt A2RT31 (mouse) carries the function and disruption phenotype with experimental evidence from that paper; UniProt Q9UGF6 (human OR5V1) carries the same function text only 'By similarity' (ECO:0000250 from A2RT31), with no tissue-specificity or disease annotation. The knockout is gene-specific for the mouse ortholog, not a paralog. The only human data in the abstract is that serum from obese patients gave lower Or5v1/Olfr110-Gs activation, which measures ligand activity, not OR5V1 expression in human liver. I read the abstract and UniProt entries, not the full paper, so whether it contains human liver expression data is unchecked.
criteria_gap: The literature verdict for OR5V1 is 'no_literature' and the only rare-cell hit (brain ependymal cell) was dismissed, but a 2026 mouse knockout paper assigns the ortholog a metabolic function in liver. Human bulk liver RNA is near zero, so the screen would only catch this through literature review. I read the UniProt annotations, not the paper itself. Flegel 2013 (PMID 23405139, read) also notes OR5V1 shares 5'UTR exons with OR12D3 in the MHC locus, so its RNA reads may be chimeric transcripts.

tissue: adipose tissue (brown fat; white fat in obesity)
claim: Mouse Otop1 is expressed in brown adipose tissue and is induced in white adipose tissue by high-fat diet and by TNF; UniProt also lists mouse thymus, heart, kidney, skin, dorsal root ganglion, adrenal, lactating mammary gland and stimulated mast cells.
source: PMID 24379350 (UniProt Q80VM9 tissue specificity and induction)
verify_reason: PMID 24379350 exists and its abstract supports induction in obese mouse white fat and by TNF in cultured adipocytes, with a metabolic phenotype in Otop1 mutant mice on high-fat diet. It is mouse only and describes an obesity (disease-state) response. The brown-fat and wider mouse tissue list is not in the abstract and rests on UniProt Q80VM9, which I did not open. No human adipose evidence.
criteria_gap: Induced expression (obesity, inflammation) is invisible to steady-state atlases; brown fat is not sampled. Mouse only.

claim: Human: UniProt curates SSX2 (and SSX1) as expressed at high level in testis and at low level in thyroid, not detected in most other tissues tested, citing PubMed:7539744. I read the UniProt entry, not the paper.
verify_reason: UniProt Q16385 (and Q16384 for SSX1) do carry 'expressed at low level in thyroid'; the SSX1 entry attributes it to PubMed:7539744. That paper is the 1995 cloning of SSX1 and SSX2 (81% identical); its abstract does not mention tissue expression, and an assay of that era is unlikely to separate SSX paralogs. The identical wording on both entries suggests one shared, non-paralog-resolved observation. Not verified in the paper's full text.
criteria_gap: The CSV's highest off-target tissue is hypothalamus (SSX2) or cerebellum (SSX1), not thyroid; a 1995 assay probably did not separate SSX paralogs, so this may be cross-hybridisation (mapping_risk is True).

claim: Mouse: MIN6 cells and mouse islets express T1R2, T1R3 and gustducin; artificial sweeteners stimulated insulin secretion via calcium and cAMP, blocked by gurmarin. Mouse only.
verify_reason: PMID 19352508 exists and says what is claimed, but it is mouse only (MIN6 line and mouse islets). T1R2 mRNA was detected by RT-PCR, while function was shown with sweeteners and gurmarin, which act on the receptor complex rather than T1R2 alone. No human data.
criteria_gap: Beta cells are a small fraction of bulk pancreas; mouse-only evidence, and the human rare-cell screen reported below_screen.

claim: Family-level, human: TAS2Rs are expressed and functional on human airway smooth muscle (bronchodilation, PMID 20972434) and in human thyrocytes, where agonists reduce TSH-dependent calcium and iodide efflux (PMID 25342133). The abstracts do not name which subtypes, so this applies to TAS2R13, TAS2R41, TAS2R50, TAS2R60, TAS2R7 and TAS2R1 only as a family-level caution; human bronchus studies that name subtypes point to TAS2R5/10/14/31 (PMID 24266887, 30365340), not these.
verify_reason: Both papers exist and say what is claimed at family level. The full text of PMID 20972434 (PMC3066567, Table 1) does name subtypes, by qRT-PCR in cultured human airway smooth muscle cells relative to ADRB2: TAS2R50 0.48, TAS2R13 0.26, TAS2R1 0.17 (all low, against 3.4 to 4.0 for TAS2R10/14/31), while TAS2R7, TAS2R41, TAS2R60 and TAS1R2 were not detected; the text states TAS2R7 'is not expressed in ASM'. So the family-level caution is wrong for TAS2R7/41/60 in airway and holds only as low transcript in cultured cells for TAS2R13/50/1. Function was shown with promiscuous agonists and TAS2R10 knockdown only. For thyroid (PMID 25342133) I could read only the abstract, which names TAS2R38 and TAS2R42 but not these genes.
criteria_gap: Low-copy GPCR expression in a specific cell type (smooth muscle, thyrocytes) sits under bulk TPM thresholds; thyroid and airway smooth muscle are not in the rare-cell screen. The CSV off-target values for these TAS2Rs (blood, white matter) do not point at these tissues.

claim: Human: UniProt curates TFDP3 as predominantly testis-expressed with a low level of expression in pancreas, citing the original cloning papers. The catalog shows 0.0 off-target TPM.
verify_reason: The UniProt Q5H9I0 line is quoted accurately, and the primary source supports it: Wang et al. 2002 (PMID 12097419) state that HCA661 (= TFDP3, per the UniProt synonym) was 'predominantly detected in testis, but not in other normal tissues, except for a weak expression in normal pancreas'. Weakened because it is a single 2002 SEREX paper, the signal is described as weak, and the abstract does not give the method (likely RT-PCR on a commercial normal-tissue panel) or say whether the product was sequenced. TFDP3 is an intronless retrogene closely related to TFDP1, so genomic DNA contamination or TFDP1 cross-amplification cannot be excluded, and pancreas RNA is prone to such artefacts. Modern atlases showing 0 TPM argue against it. PMID 16418725's abstract says nothing about tissue distribution. Primary full texts were not read.
criteria_gap: Gene-specific assays in the original papers report low pancreas signal that the RNA atlases show as zero; the primary papers were not opened, so the method and level are unverified.

claim: Human: immunohistochemistry on a tissue array with an anti-C-terminal DEFB106 antibody located native protein in epididymis, bone marrow and skin (hair follicle cells). The staining was nuclear, which is odd for a secreted defensin, so antibody specificity is uncertain.
verify_reason: The abstract of PMID 24189797 does say 'native DEFB106 was located in the epididymis, bone marrow and skin'. The hair-follicle and nuclear-staining details are not in the abstract and I could not verify them in the full text. The evidence is a single in-house antibody on a tissue array with no knockout or orthogonal validation mentioned, so specificity for DEFB106 over other beta-defensins is not established; donor status of the array is not stated in the abstract.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle and bone marrow are outside the bulk and rare-cell panels. This is protein-level evidence despite near-zero RNA, from a single antibody without knockout validation.

cell_type: differentiating hair shaft keratinocytes above the bulb (not outer root sheath or interfollicular epidermis)
claim: In mouse, Hoxc12 is expressed in the epithelial compartment of developing and postnatally cycling hair follicles, in a domain distal to and slightly overlapping Hoxc13, consistent with a role in hair shaft differentiation. Mouse only; no knockout phenotype was found.
verify_reason: The abstract of PMID 11960714 supports the claim as written: Hoxc12 RNA in the epidermal part of developing and cycling mouse hair follicles, excluding outer root sheath and interfollicular epidermis, with a domain distal to and overlapping Hoxc13 at the upper bulb, compared directly against Hoxc13. It is mouse only, RNA only, with no functional or knockout data and no human evidence; the link to the human bulk-skin TPM is inference.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle is not a separate tissue in the bulk panels or the rare-cell screen. The 5.39 TPM skin value probably reflects follicle-restricted expression diluted in bulk skin, so per-cell expression in anagen follicles may be much higher. Nail unit is likewise unsampled.

claim: Human: UniProt/GeneCards annotate KAP1.4 as expressed in the middle and upper hair cortex (keratogenous zone), a structural matrix protein cross-linking hair keratins. Related KAP1 members were shown by in situ hybridization in the differentiated hair cortex.
verify_reason: The cited GeneCards page was not opened by the finder and is a secondary source. The primary source behind the UniProt P0C5Y4 annotation is PMID 11279113 (Rogers 2001), whose abstract reports in situ data only for 'single members of five different KAP multigene families', all in the upper hair cortex, plus 3'-specific cDNA screening of a scalp library. The abstract does not say KAP1.4 was the KAP1 member probed, and the other KAP1 in situ work the finder alludes to used a conserved probe across four KAP1 members. Hair-cortex expression is very likely real, but it is not shown to be specific to this gene among near-identical KAP1 copies.
criteria_gap: Hair cortex is not sampled in bulk or rare-cell panels; only 1.1 TPM in bulk skin. Mapping risk among near-identical KAP1 copies.

claim: Human: characterization of the 21q22.1 KAP domain found 6 of 7 high-sulfur KAP genes (families KAP11, KAP13, KAP15, KAP23) expressed in the hair-forming compartment by scalp cDNA isolation and in situ hybridization. The abstract does not say which KAP13 members were positive, so this is family-level for KRTAP13-3.
best_source: PMID 12359730 (abstract only; member-level table in full text not checked)
verify_reason: PMID 12359730 abstract exists and says 6 of the 7 high-sulfur KAP genes (KAP11, KAP13, KAP15, KAP23 families) were expressed in the hair-forming compartment, without naming members. One high-sulfur gene was not detected and it could be this one. I could not open the full text (publisher blocked), UniProt Q3SY46 has no tissue annotation, and a PubMed search found no human KRTAP13-3-specific expression paper. Family-level only, as the finder already said.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle absent from all panels; the catalog shows 0.0 off-target TPM, so a hair-restricted transcript would be invisible.

claim: Human: same 21q22.1 study; 6 of 7 high-sulfur KAP genes including the KAP13 family were expressed in the hair-forming compartment. Family-level evidence for KRTAP13-4; no gene-specific paper was found.
verify_reason: Same as KRTAP13-3: PMID 12359730 abstract gives 6 of 7 high-sulfur genes expressed in the hair-forming compartment with no member list; full text not accessible; UniProt Q3LI77 has no tissue annotation; no gene-specific human paper found. The claim is real at family level but unproven for this gene.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle not sampled. Bulk TPM is 0.33 but nTPM is 6.4 (adipose), an unexplained discrepancy that no paper addresses.

claim: Human: 11 of 17 high glycine-tyrosine KAP genes at 21q22.1 (families KAP6-8 and KAP19-22) were expressed in the hair-forming compartment by scalp cDNA isolation and in situ hybridization. This applies at family level to KRTAP19-2, KRTAP19-4, KRTAP19-6, KRTAP19-7 and KRTAP19-8; the abstract does not list which members were positive (6 of 17 were not detected).
verify_reason: PMID 12359730 abstract confirms 11 of 17 high glycine-tyrosine KAP genes (KAP6-8, KAP19-22) were expressed in the hair-forming compartment and 6 were not, without naming them. With 6 of 17 negative, the chance that any given KRTAP19 member was undetected is substantial. Full text not accessible; UniProt Q3LHN2 has no tissue annotation. Family-level only; the 'cortex matrix' location is not in the abstract.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle is absent from bulk and rare-cell panels, so all five KRTAP19 entries in this batch show under 1 TPM in skin. Blood values for KRTAP19-2 and KRTAP19-8 are likely mapping artefacts rather than the true normal site.

claim: Human, family-level: scalp cDNA isolation and in situ hybridization of all 21q22.1 KAP genes showed expression of 11 of the 17 high glycine-tyrosine genes (families KAP6-8, KAP19-22) in the hair-forming compartment (Rogers 2002). The abstract does not say which members were positive.
verify_reason: Rogers 2002 abstract (PMID 12359730) confirms 17 high glycine-tyrosine genes in families KAP6-8 and KAP19-22, of which 11 were expressed in the hair-forming compartment; 6 were not, and the abstract does not name them. UniProt Q3LI63 has no tissue annotation and protein existence is 'Inferred from homology', consistent with this member possibly being among the unexpressed ones. Full text was not accessible (publisher 403). Family-level only.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle is absent from bulk panels and the rare-cell screen. Per-gene in situ results need the full text; only the abstract was read.

claim: Human, family-level: 11 of 17 high glycine-tyrosine KAP genes on 21q22.1 (KAP6-8, KAP19-22) were expressed in the hair-forming compartment by scalp cDNA isolation and in situ hybridization (Rogers 2002); member-level result not given in the abstract.
verify_reason: Rogers 2002 abstract gives only the 11-of-17 family-level count; the member-level result is not in the abstract and the full text was not accessible. UniProt Q3LI61 has no tissue annotation, though protein existence is 'Evidence at protein level', which mildly favours real expression. Hair-only in any case.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle is not sampled; per-gene result needs the full text.

claim: Human, family-level: 11 of 17 high glycine-tyrosine KAP genes on 21q22.1 (including the KAP21 family) were expressed in the hair-forming compartment (Rogers 2002); member-level result not in the abstract.
verify_reason: Rogers 2002 abstract supports only the family-level 11-of-17 statement; which members were positive is not stated and the full text was not accessible. UniProt Q3LI58 has no tissue annotation and is 'Inferred from homology', so this member may be one of the 6 unexpressed genes.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle is not sampled; per-gene result needs the full text. Catalog's top tissue (blood) is unrelated.

claim: Human, family-level: 11 of 17 high glycine-tyrosine KAP genes on 21q22.1 (including the KAP21 family) were expressed in the hair-forming compartment (Rogers 2002); member-level result not in the abstract.
verify_reason: Family-level only from the Rogers 2002 abstract (11 of 17 expressed, members unnamed); full text not accessible. UniProt Q3LI59 has no tissue annotation; protein existence is 'Evidence at protein level'. Hair-only in any case.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle is not sampled; per-gene result needs the full text.

claim: Human, family-level: 11 of 17 high glycine-tyrosine KAP genes on 21q22.1 (including the KAP22 family) were expressed in the hair-forming compartment (Rogers 2002); member-level result not in the abstract.
verify_reason: Family-level only: Rogers 2002 abstract names the KAP22 family but not which members were among the 11 expressed; full text not accessible. UniProt Q3MIV0 has no tissue annotation and is 'Inferred from homology', so it may be among the 6 unexpressed genes.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle is not sampled; per-gene result needs the full text.

claim: Human, family-level: KAP23 is one of four high sulfur KAP families on 21q22.1, of which 6 of 7 genes were expressed in the hair-forming compartment by scalp cDNA isolation and in situ hybridization (Rogers 2002); the abstract does not name the positive members.
verify_reason: Rogers 2002 abstract confirms KAP23 is one of four high sulfur families (KAP11, KAP13, KAP15, KAP23) and that 6 of the 7 high sulfur genes were expressed in the hair-forming compartment, but does not say which one was negative; full text not accessible. UniProt A1A580 has no tissue annotation; 'Evidence at protein level'. Six-in-seven odds favour expression, but it is not demonstrated per gene. Hair-only.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle is not sampled; per-gene result needs the full text. Catalog's top tissue (hypothalamus, 0.2 TPM) is unrelated.

claim: Human: UniProt Q9BYQ7 annotates expression in hair follicles (citing Kariya 2005, PMID 15955084); KAP4 cDNAs were isolated from a human scalp library and in situ hybridization of representative members of five chromosome 17q12-21 KAP families localised mRNA to the upper cortex of the hair shaft (Rogers 2001). The in situ result is per family, not shown specifically for KAP4.1 in the abstract.
verify_reason: Rogers 2001 abstract (PMID 11279113) confirms 37 KAP genes on 17q12-21, 26 cDNAs from a human scalp library, and in situ for 'single members of five different KAP multigene families' in the upper cortex; it does not name KAP4.1 as a cDNA-positive or in situ-probed member. UniProt Q9BYQ7 does say 'Expressed in the hair follicles' citing Kariya 2005 (PMID 15955084), but that paper's abstract is about KAP4 size polymorphisms, not an expression study. So hair-follicle expression is plausible and curated, but cortex localisation is family-level and the member-level assay is not shown. Hair-only; nothing in a vital tissue.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle cortex is absent from bulk panels and the rare-cell screen; the catalog's top off-target tissue (blood) is unrelated to the documented site.

claim: Human, family-level only: KAP4 family genes on 17q12-21 are scalp-expressed with mRNA in the upper hair cortex (Rogers 2001); KRTAP4-16 (formerly annotated pseudogene KRTAP4P1) has no gene-specific expression study that I found and UniProt G5E9R7 lists no tissue specificity.
verify_reason: Pure family inference. Rogers 2001 abstract does not name this gene (it was annotated as a pseudogene, KRTAP4P1, at the time), and UniProt G5E9R7 has no tissue-specificity annotation. No gene-specific expression evidence exists in the cited source; the claim itself concedes this.
criteria_gap: Hair follicle is not sampled; inference rests on family membership, and the cerebral cortex bulk value is on a mapping-risk gene.

claim: Human: RT-PCR showed expression in hair root (not skin) and also in brain and skeletal muscle (Yahagi 2004; UniProt Q6L8G5). The catalog's top off-target tissue is skin; brain and skeletal muscle are not reflected.
verify_reason: The source does say it: UniProt Q6L8G5 (citing PMID 15144888) reads 'Expressed in hair root but not in skin. Expressed also in brain and skeletal muscle'. Hair root part stands. Brain/skeletal-muscle part rests on one non-quantitative RT-PCR of a single-exon gene (genomic DNA contamination indistinguishable from transcript) in a near-identical family, with no sequencing/in situ/protein confirmation in the abstract and no replication; the RNA atlases do not show it. Unconfirmed lead rather than documented expression. Full text not opened.
criteria_gap: Hair root is not in any panel; gene-specific RT-PCR reports brain and skeletal muscle expression that the atlas values (mapping-risk gene in a near-identical KRTAP5 family) do not show.

claim: Human: RT-PCR showed expression in hair root (not skin) and also in liver and skeletal muscle (Yahagi 2004; UniProt Q6L8G9). This independently agrees with the catalog's top off-target tissue being liver (2.44 TPM), so that signal may be real rather than a mapping artefact.
verify_reason: The source does say it: UniProt Q6L8G9 (citing PMID 15144888) reads 'Expressed in hair root and not in skin. Expressed also in liver and skeletal muscle'. Hair root part stands. The liver/skeletal-muscle part is weaker than claimed: it is a single non-quantitative RT-PCR (abstract mentions no sequencing, in situ or protein), on a single-exon gene where genomic DNA carry-over gives the same amplicon as cDNA, in a near-identical family. It has not been independently replicated, and a 2.4 TPM mapping-risk bulk value is not independent confirmation. Treat as an unconfirmed lead, not documented vital-tissue expression. Full text not opened (abstract plus UniProt curation only).
criteria_gap: Hair root is not in any panel; and the liver/skeletal-muscle bulk signal is below the screen threshold and flagged mapping-risk, so a gene-specific RT-PCR confirmation in two vital tissues is not captured.

claim: Human, family-level: 11 of 17 high glycine-tyrosine KAP genes on 21q22.1 (including the KAP6 family) were expressed in the hair-forming compartment by scalp cDNA isolation and in situ hybridization (Rogers 2002); member-level result not in the abstract.
verify_reason: Rogers 2002 abstract supports the family-level claim (KAP6 family included; 11 of 17 high glycine-tyrosine genes expressed) but not the member-level result; full text not accessible. UniProt Q3LI64 has no tissue annotation; protein existence is 'Evidence at protein level'. Likely genuinely hair-expressed, but not shown per gene in what I could read. Hair-only.

claim: Human: the HPA gene record lists OR13A1 under tissue cell type enrichment as 'Spleen - B-cells', with a lymphoma cell-line cluster annotated 'humoral immune response', which suggests the 14.87 TPM blood signal in the CSV is B-lineage transcription. verify_reason: The HPA record (ENSG00000256574) exists and does say what was quoted: tissue cell type enrichment 'Spleen - B-cells (Spleen)', cell line cluster 'Cluster 46: Lymphoma - Humoral immune response', transcript-level evidence only, single-cell 1.6 nCPM in papillary tip epithelial cells and 2.3 nCPM in cerebellar Purkinje nuclei. HPA's sorted blood cell data, which include naive and memory B cells, list OR13A1 as 'Not detected in immune cells' with blood lineage 'Not detected', so the record gives no direct support for the blood signal being B-lineage transcription. The 'Spleen - B-cells' label is not a measurement in B cells: it is a correlation of bulk spleen RNA with B-cell marker genes across samples. The lymphoma signal is a tumor cell line at 4.1 nTPM, which is not normal tissue. Bulk tissue specificity is 'Low tissue specificity', tissue cluster 'Non-specific - Transcription', protein 'Not detected'. All of this is short-read RNA quantification of an olfactory receptor gene with no gene-specific assay (no qRT-PCR, in situ or antibody), so read mis-assignment or an overlapping transcript cannot be excluded. claim: Human: OR4E2 circulating RNA was measurable by RT-qPCR and differed between mild gestational hypothyroidism and healthy pregnancy, correlating negatively with TSH and normalising after levothyroxine. This suggests hormone-responsive expression in a blood-derived sample, in pregnant women only.
best_source: PMID 38069004 (Hirata et al., Int J Mol Sci 2023; PMC10706743)
verify_reason: The source exists and the claim is accurately hedged, but it is weak as normal-tissue evidence. Full text (PMC10706743): whole-blood RNA in PAXgene tubes from pregnant women only, 24 subjects (11 healthy-thyroid, 7 untreated mild gestational hypothyroidism, 6 levothyroxine-treated). RT-qPCR relative expression of OR4E2 differed between groups (p<0.05) and correlated negatively with TSH (r=-0.44); OR4E2 was not detectable in one sample. This is a cross-sectional association, not demonstrated hormone induction: the treated group is different women, not the same women before and after. No cell of origin, no amplicon sequencing or protein, and OR4E2 is a single-exon gene so genomic DNA carry-over is a concern. It adds nothing beyond the 0.72 TPM blood value the catalog already has.
criteria_gap: The catalog already has 0.72 TPM in blood; the paper adds that the level may be hormone-dependent (induced rather than constitutive), which a steady-state atlas would not capture. Cell of origin is not identified and no amplicon sequencing is mentioned in the abstract.

claim: Human: RNA-seq of peripheral blood from six women with anorexia nervosa found OR52J3 among olfactory receptor genes up-regulated more than two-fold after weight restoration, suggesting state-dependent expression in blood. Patient samples only, no healthy control baseline in the abstract.
verify_reason: The source exists (Kim et al. 2013, PMC3805820) and says OR52J3 was up-regulated more than two-fold in whole blood after weight restoration in six women with anorexia nervosa. There are no healthy controls, the authors call the results preliminary, and the full text notes that transcripts with zero read counts at one time point produced large fold-changes, which points to very low absolute counts. There was no qRT-PCR or other orthogonal validation. Three of the four olfactory receptors named (OR51L1, OR51A4, OR51A2) and OR52J3 all sit in the chromosome 11p15 cluster beside the beta-globin locus, so read-through or mis-mapped reads from the very abundant globin transcripts in whole blood are a plausible artifact; that explanation is my inference, not something the paper tests. This is not evidence of physiological induced expression in normal blood cells.
criteria_gap: The catalog's peak for OR52J3 is 0.2 TPM in cerebral cortex with blood not flagged; constitutive bulk and sorted immune-cell RNA would miss expression that varies with nutritional or metabolic state.

claim: Human: the curated UniProt entry for PRAME (P78395) records that PRAME is up-regulated by interferon gamma and bacterial PAMPs, citing PMID 23460923. This is inducible rather than constitutive expression.
verify_reason: The UniProt induction annotation exists and cites PMID 23460923, but the paper (Wadelin 2013, PLoS One; abstract and full text opened) shows induction only in leukaemic cell lines, mainly HL60, with U937 used for localisation. No primary PBMC, monocytes, neutrophils or healthy-donor leukocytes were tested. IFN-gamma or LPS alone did not significantly change PRAME; induction needed a PAMP plus IFN-gamma and was transient. The authors only speculate that inducibility might explain low levels in normal tissue. This is not evidence of expression in normal activated immune cells.
criteria_gap: The bulk, sorted immune-cell and single-cell panels are resting-state; none capture interferon- or PAMP-stimulated cells. COVERAGE CAVEAT FOR THIS WHOLE BATCH: the session's shared web search budget ran out after one search, so every other gene was checked only against its UniProt curated annotation (tissue specificity, function, induction, disease), not a literature search. I read the UniProt annotation only, not the cited paper.

claim: Mouse: a lymphocyte-specific Spo11 transcript (alternative 5' exon) is induced more than eightfold by RT-PCR in LPS/cytokine-stimulated B cells undergoing class switching. However, Spo11-deficient mice have normal somatic hypermutation and class switching, so the induced transcript has no required function.
source: PMID 11591116 and PMID 10873300 (Tokuyama & Tokuyama, Cell Immunol 2001/2000); PMID 11807770 (Klein et al., Eur J Immunol 2002)
best_source: PMID 11807770 (Klein et al., Eur J Immunol 2002) for the knockout; PMID 11591116 for the induced transcript
verify_reason: All three sources exist and match. PMID 10873300 (Tokuyama & Tokuyama, Cell Immunol 2000): mouse Spo11 detected by RT-PCR on day 3 in normal mu+ B cells under IgA/IgG1 class-switch stimuli. PMID 11591116 (same authors, 2001): lymphocyte-derived Spo11 cDNA with a novel 5' portion, exons 2-12 identical to testis form, 'strongly induced (above eightfold)' with LPS + retinoic acid + IL-4; note this paper also claims antisense oligo inhibited class switching 60-90%, which the finding omitted. PMID 11807770 (Klein et al., Eur J Immunol 2002): Spo11-/- mice have normal somatic hypermutation and normal serum levels of all Ig isotypes, 'Spo11 is not required for Ig hypermutation or class switch recombination', which contradicts the antisense result and removes any required function. Spo11 is single-copy and the cDNA was sequenced, so the assay is gene-specific, but the evidence is mouse only, in vitro stimulated cells, RT-PCR without protein, from a single two-author group and not independently replicated; no human activated-B-cell data. Accurately described by the finder as low priority.
criteria_gap: Sorted immune-cell RNA in the screen is from resting cells; induced expression in activated B cells would not be seen. Evidence is mouse RT-PCR only and the knockout argues against functional relevance, so this is low priority.

claim: UniProt annotates human TRIM60 (Q495X7) as an E3 SUMO ligase that SUMOylates TAB2 and suppresses NF-kB and MAPK signalling, citing PMID 33184450. best_source: PMID 33184450 (Gu et al., Cell Mol Immunol 2021;18:1981, PMC8322076); UniProt Q8VI40 also notes mouse Trim60 expression is restricted to embryos up to the 8-cell stage (PMID 11424210)
verify_reason: The sources exist and say what is claimed: UniProt Q495X7 and Q8VI40 both carry the TAB2 SUMOylation function citing PMID 33184450, and the mouse entry carries the knockout phenotype. But the paper (Gu et al., Cell Mol Immunol 2021, PMC8322076) is entirely mouse or overexpression: Trim60 knockout mice, mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages, mouse embryonic fibroblasts, the RAW 264.7 mouse macrophage line, and tagged TRIM60 transfected into HEK293T. No expression of endogenous TRIM60 in human macrophages or any normal adult human tissue is shown, and the human UniProt function is inferred from the mouse work. One correction to the claim: the paper's full text says knockout mice were more susceptible to LPS shock but more resistant to Listeria, not simply an 'elevated response' to both. The assay is gene-specific (knockout, shRNA with qPCR), so this is a real mouse macrophage function with no human normal-tissue evidence.
criteria_gap: The catalog's literature verdict is no_normal_expression_evidence and the highest off-target value is 0.5 TPM in blood; a functional role in immune signalling at low or induced RNA levels is not visible to steady-state bulk or sorted-cell RNA thresholds. No copy-specific data for USP17L3, as the claim itself concedes.
criteria_gap: Induced, transient expression is invisible to resting-tissue atlases, and the copies are too similar for copy-specific quantification.

claim: Human, family-level: same evidence as USP17L1 (IL-4/IL-6-inducible, cell-cycle-regulated USP17 family). There is no literature specific to USP17L4; its UniProt entry has no functional annotation.
verify_reason: The source is real but concerns DUB-3 (USP17L2), with induction reported alongside cell lines rather than normal adult human tissue. Nothing in it is specific to USP17L4; the finding is extrapolation from a near-identical family member.
criteria_gap: Induced, transient expression is invisible to resting-tissue atlases, and the copies are too similar for copy-specific quantification.

claim: Human, family-level: same evidence as USP17L1 (IL-4/IL-6-inducible, cell-cycle-regulated USP17 family). There is no literature specific to USP17L7; the CSV's top off-target tissue is already blood (1.52 TPM), consistent with an immune-cell signal.
verify_reason: The source is real but concerns DUB-3 (USP17L2), with induction reported alongside cell lines rather than normal adult human tissue. Nothing in it is specific to USP17L7. The catalog's 1.52 TPM blood value is multi-mapping-prone and does not independently corroborate a copy-specific immune signal.
criteria_gap: Induced, transient expression is invisible to resting-tissue atlases, and the copies are too similar for copy-specific quantification.

claim: Human cell lines: BPIFB6 silencing fragments the Golgi, alters retrograde and anterograde trafficking, and suppresses enterovirus replication, indicating a secretory-pathway function in somatic cells.
verify_reason: The abstract of PMID 26962226 confirms the claim: BPIFB6 is ER-localised, and RNAi silencing causes Golgi fragmentation, altered retrograde and anterograde trafficking, and suppressed replication of coxsackievirus B, poliovirus and EV71. The RNAi is gene-specific and the phenotype is opposite to BPIFB3's. The evidence is from cultured cell lines only, which says nothing about which normal adult tissues express the protein. It is a mechanism, not normal-tissue expression.
criteria_gap: A cell-biological role in non-germ cells with no in vivo tissue assigned; not covered by the literature review. Title confirmed via PubMed; the detail comes from a search summary, not the abstract.

cell_type: salivary duct epithelium, serous and mucous acini; also nerves and some endothelium within the gland
claim: Human: CABS1 protein was detected in submandibular gland by Western blot, immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence with monoclonal antibodies, and in saliva and serum by Western blot. The authors flag antibody caveats: several bands were nonspecific, isotype controls were not clean, and mass spectrometry failed to sequence CABS1 from gland or saliva.
verify_reason: Source opened (Reyes-Serratos et al., PLoS One 2024) and it says what the claim says, caveats included: human submandibular gland by Western blot, IHC and IF; saliva and serum by Western blot only. Weakened rather than confirmed because the protein identity is not orthogonally established: the authors could not sequence CABS1 from gland or saliva by mass spectrometry, many monoclonal bands in saliva looked nonspecific, and the 13G3 isotype control gave a band at 64 kDa overlapping the signal. The tissue is adult human but not from healthy donors: Western blot and IHC used grossly or morphologically normal areas of glands resected for squamous carcinoma, and IF used two carcinoma resections plus two Sjogren's syndrome glands. Serum was a pilot on one pooled sample from a single 30-year-old man. I read only the first 100,000 characters of the page.
criteria_gap: The CSV already shows salivary gland as the top off-target tissue (3.0 TPM, 3.9 nTPM), which sits near the pass threshold. This paper adds protein-level evidence in a secretory tissue plus a secreted form in saliva and serum, which the RNA value alone does not show.

claim: Human: an earlier paper from the same group reported that CABS1, previously thought testis-only, is also expressed in salivary glands and lung, and that peptides from its C-terminal region are anti-inflammatory in rodent models. I saw this only as a search-result summary; the lung claim was not confirmed in the 2024 follow-up that I did read.
best_source: PMID 25632019, PMC4386001, DOI 10.1152/ajpregu.00153.2014 (abstract only read); follow-up PMID 38753592
verify_reason: The paper exists (St Laurent et al., Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol 2015, PMID 25632019). I could read only the abstract via Europe PMC; full text was blocked. The abstract states: 'Using Western blot and PCR, we discovered that the human protein CABS1, previously thought to only be expressed in the testes, is also expressed in the salivary glands and lung, in a tissue-specific manner.' So the claim matches the abstract and is about human CABS1. Weakened because I could not check tissue source, donor status, antibody type or whether PCR products were sequenced, and the same group's 2024 follow-up did not study lung and raised specificity problems with their CABS1 antibodies. The lung claim rests on this one unreplicated report; human/adult/normal is assumed from the abstract, not verified.
criteria_gap: Lung is in the bulk panels but the reported expression may be confined to a minor cell population or to protein; the screen has no literature verdict for this gene.

claim: Human: a 27 kDa salivary CABS1 band was reported to rise with salivary cortisol during acute and exam stress. The 2024 follow-up from the same group could not confirm that this 27 kDa form is CABS1, so the stress link is weak. Seen only as a search-result summary.
best_source: PMID 28381457, PMC5495925, DOI 10.1152/ajpregu.00393.2016 (abstract only read); contradicted in part by PMID 38753592
verify_reason: The paper exists (Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol 2017, PMID 28381457); only the abstract was readable.
